findings.title: Double interpolation of queries in shard splitting path
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery now calls applyTemplateVariables on each query at line 52, but later, when it invokes runSplitQuery (line 163), runSplitQuery also applies applyTemplateVariables (querySplitting.ts line 299). This causes every query to be interpolated twice. In particular, ad hoc filters (request.filters) are applied twice, leading to duplicated filter matchers and invalid Loki expressions. This also affects any non-idempotent interpolation. The fix is to interpolate only once: either remove interpolation from runShardSplitQuery and rely on runSplitQuery, or add a flag to runSplitQuery to skip interpolation when targets are already interpolated.

findings.title: Interpolation before querySupportsSplitting bypasses $__range detection
findings.body: The new .map() call interpolates each query before partition(queries, ...) on line 300. querySupportsSplitting (line 282) uses isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr) to identify queries containing $__range and avoid splitting them. After interpolation, $__range is replaced with a concrete duration (e.g., 2d), so isQueryWithRangeVariable no longer detects it, and such queries are split despite the explicit comment explaining why they should not be. This produces incorrect subqueries with the full range baked into each split interval. The check should be performed on the original query.expr before interpolation, or the raw expr must be preserved for this decision.

findings.title: RequestSupportsSharding check bypassed for $__range due to early interpolation
findings.body: Like in querySplitting, runShardSplitQuery now interpolates queries at line 52 before splitQueriesByStreamShard is called on line 54. Inside splitQueriesByStreamShard, groupTargetsByQueryType calls requestSupportsSharding (line 243), which likely checks for $__range via isQueryWithRangeVariable. Because the expression has been interpolated, $__range is no longer present, so queries that should not be sharded are incorrectly considered shardable. This can lead to shard splitting of queries with range variables, producing wrong results. The raw expression must be used for the sharding eligibility check.

findings.title: Missing tests for double interpolation and range variable bypass
findings.body: The new interpolation tests use mock replace functions that are idempotent for the specific variables, so they do not reveal double interpolation (especially duplicate ad hoc filters) or the fact that $__range detection is bypassed after interpolation. Tests should cover a query with $__range to ensure it is not split, and a query with ad hoc filters to verify filters are applied only once. Without these, the regressions introduced by this PR may go unnoticed.
